name: ntfy
description: Simple HTTP-based pub-sub notification service. Send push notifications to your phone or desktop via scripts.
summary: ntfy v2.28.0 (2026-08-27) is a hardening release focused on bounding cache replay costs, adding size limits for message titles (1 KB) and tags (512 bytes), capping single cache replays at 10 MB per topic, and applying visitor bandwidth limits to poll requests. Recent releases (v2.25.0–v2.27.0) also added password reset via emailed magic link, email-based login, PostgreSQL support graduation from experimental, message template security hardening, and a fail2ban-compatible abuse ban-feed. Full release notes are available at https://github.com/binwiederhier/ntfy/releases.

answers.What is the current license?: Apache 2.0 (server) and GPL-2.0 (client); dual-licensed — check repository for specifics
answers.Is the project actively maintained?: Yes — multiple releases in 2026, most recently v2.28.0 on 2026-08-27
answers.Does it support authentication and acces: Yes — username/password, access tokens, email-based login, and per-topic access control

breaking_excerpts: Message title now limited to 1 KB and all tags combined to 512 bytes; requests exceeding these limits are rejected with HTTP 400 (error codes 40057/40058).
visitor-attachment-daily-bandwidth-limit now also covers cache replay from poll requests; heavy pollers consume the same budget as attachment downloads, so operators may need to raise the limit.
Message cache databases from ntfy older than v1.10.0 (November 2021) can no longer be migrated; upgrade via an older ntfy version first or delete the cache database.

alternatives.name: Pushover
alternatives.review: Paid SaaS, simple API, iOS/Android apps.

alternatives.name: Gotify
alternatives.review: Self-hosted only, real-time push via WebSocket.

alternatives.name: Apprise
alternatives.review: Apprise is a versatile open-source notification library supporting 80+ services but is a library/CLI tool rather than a standalone pub-sub server.

alternatives.name: Pushbullet
alternatives.review: Pushbullet provides cross-device notifications with file sharing features but is closed-source, cloud-only, and has reduced its free tier significantly over time.

alternatives.name: Cabot
alternatives.review: Cabot is a self-hosted alerting and monitoring tool with notification support but is more complex and focused on ops alerting rather than general-purpose push notifications.
